report.summary: Recommendation: needs review. Not enough evidence: cannot tell whether py reaches level 2. Estimated levels: py level 1 (needs 2), sql level 3 (needs 3), ds level 2 (needs 2). Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes looking up a key in a hash table (dict/set) checks the stored entries one by one, so membership and lookup are O(n) on average, like a list. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes that after an exception is caught, execution goes back to the try block and continues with the line after the one that raised. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes list.sort() returns the sorted list, not knowing it sorts in place and returns None (unlike sorted(), which returns a new list). Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes hash table operations are O(1) guaranteed in every case, ignoring that many collisions (a poor hash function or adversarial keys) degrade lookups towards O(n). Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes that when two different keys hash to the same value or slot, the newer key overwrites the older one, so colliding keys cannot both be stored. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes other sessions see a transaction's changes as soon as each statement runs, before COMMIT.
